I counted the actual repetitions: 5 open(&decl, &ctx) ceremonies, 3 UnexpectedManifestVersion from/to guards (Claude said 4 — there's no guard in the pre-state step; he over-counted by one), and 4 excluded/resolver_batched re-filter continue sites. Not load-bearing either way, but the point stands: the duplication is the primary defect, and my step-extraction framing kept the continue-guards inside the steps. Claude's "classify once into an ordered op list → single executor" is the real fix, and the &mut cx bag vs returned-values critique is a fair Rust-idiom call. Conceded.

WalkBookkeeping was a bag, not owned stages. Conceded — with one nuance to hand Claude (below).

S4's deny-list default was fail-open in the wrong place. The details field gets persisted into the receipt, which gets committed to the repo by the workflow. A deny-list miss is a credential in git history forever. Allow-list is the right default. Conceded.

Templates path. callisto-graph/Cargo.toml has no include/exclude (I checked), so crate-root templates/ would ship only if git-tracked — a real verification hazard for a published crate. Claude's gotcha is valid; the fix is src/templates/, which makes it moot.

The scanner exists. crates/callisto-graph/tests/architecture.rs is a real source-scanning enforcement test (pattern B: no hand-parsed manifests, with allowlist + brace-depth test-stripping). I never read it — my doc hedged "add a rule" without the vehicle. S2's fix fits it naturally.

Claude also self-corrected his own from-groups "zero callers" error, and the verified state (4 callers, both inline sites confirmed inside #[cfg(test)] blocks) matches the roadmap's "close before a production caller appears" — so S3 stands as written.

Where Claude is missing or wrong
The .yml/actionlint point is self-undermining. The templates contain __BRANCH__ and uses: .../callisto-action@__COMMIT__ placeholders. @__COMMIT__ is not a valid uses ref, so actionlint cannot lint the template file — it can only lint the rendered output. The right pattern is: .tmpl suffix (a placeholder file can't be mistaken for a real workflow), insta snapshot of rendered bytes, plus a lint/parse check on the rendered artifact. And "no template engine" was never a disagreement — my doc already said include_str! + string replace, which is exactly the plain mechanism he's endorsing. So this "correction" corrects nothing and would regress the file extension.

S1 conflates a code fix with an owner decision. resolve_unique is public API on the published MIT crate (0.10.0 on crates.io). Two things Claude skips: (a) direction — if workspace.json documents status attribution at the display level (bare-as-wildcard being the intended display semantics), then the version path is the outlier, and deleting the display resolver inverts documented behavior. The paired fixture answers this; run it before choosing which side migrates. (b) surface — removal/deprecation of published API is a check-api/semver event and, per the house style (ROAD-TO-V1 already queues four migration notices for the retired callisto-* crates), a deprecation + notice, not a silent deletion. Fine to recommend removal; it's D01's to decide.

R2 is missing the constraint that actually makes "single executor" safe. The byte-identity anchor isn't just about which files change — it's per-file operation order: in the batched loop a file gets bump, then all its rewrites, then exactly one persist. A "classify once, execute once" dispatch must encode per-file op order (bump → rewrites → single persist) as data, or workspace-inherited/dual-write manifests can emit different bytes even with the same final values. Claude's shape is right; the implementer needs this spelled out or they'll find it only via test failures.

R1's owned stages have a subtlety: the per-path loop is incremental and order-dependent — a path's bare-vs-prefixed identity depends on names seen earlier in path-sorted order, so the Discovered → Identified stage is still one loop with local scratch, returning (decls, index, promoted_siblings). Owned stages reshape the data boundary, not the loop. (Also: promoted_siblings is consumed by a later stage, so it's an output of the identity stage, not scratch — minor, but it decides the return type.)

R3, one addition: the insta snapshot should capture the serialized intent (digest covers correctness) and the ordered operation-ID list — the digest proves stability, but the ID list makes the DAG diff readable in PR review.

S4, one addition: the allow-list needs a last-resort class (exit code, HTTP status line, last line) so a novel-but-safe failure doesn't leave the user with zero signal — fail-closed on credentials, never blind on diagnosis. And since the allow-list shapes persisted wire, it belongs in the spec, versioned.

Bottom line
Claude's corrections are substantively right on five of six points and improve the doc — adopt: drop R4, re-frame R2 (duplication helpers + data-driven dispatch, returned values), owned stages in R1, allow-list in S4, src/templates/, insta-first for R1/R3/R5, architecture.rs as the S2 vehicle, R2-first ordering. Overrule: the .yml/actionlint point (keep .tmpl, lint rendered output), and qualify S1 (spec-direction + deprecation, owner decision) and S4 (last-resort class).

content.text:
Qwen's pushback is mostly right, and it improves the plan. I'd adopt most of it, concede one miscount of mine, and keep one judgement call as it is.

**Where Qwen is right**
- **My count was off.** There are 3 `UnexpectedManifestVersion` guards, not 4. The pre-state step has none.
- **Per-file operation order is the missing R2 constraint.** In the batched loop a file gets its bump, then all its rewrites, then exactly one `persist`. The classified op list must encode that order as data. Otherwise a file with a bump and rewrites, such as a dual-write manifest, can come out with different bytes even when the final values match. It belongs in the R2 brief.
- **R1's stages are one incremental, order-dependent loop.** A path's bare or prefixed identity depends on names seen earlier in path-sorted order. Owned stages reshape the data boundary, not the loop. `promoted_siblings` is an output of the identity stage, not scratch.
- **`.yml`:** I recommended it so actionlint could lint the templates. That was weak, because the templates live in `src/templates/`, not `.github/workflows`, so actionlint wouldn't scan them anyway, and a placeholder file shouldn't pass for a real workflow. Use `.tmpl`, and lint the rendered output, which the contract tests already consume. I said "no template engine" and Qwen already agreed, so that point corrected nothing.
- **R3 snapshot:** capture the serialized intent plus the ordered operation-ID list. The digest proves stability, and the ID list makes the DAG diff readable in review.
- **S4 allow-list:** it needs a last-resort class (exit code, HTTP status line) so a novel failure still gives some signal. It persists into the receipt and gets committed, so it should be versioned in the spec.
- **S1:** deprecation plus a notice is the house style for a published API, not silent removal. Also run the paired fixture first, because the documented display-level semantics might make the version path the outlier. That is a D01 owner decision.

**Qwen's earlier concessions stand:** drop R4, `src/templates/` rather than a crate-root `templates/`, and use `architecture.rs` as the S2 vehicle.

**Merged plan**
1. **R2:** helpers (`open_canonical`, `write_version_guarded`), then one ordered op list per file (bump, rewrites, single persist), then a single executor. Steps return values rather than sharing a context. The existing byte-identity tests are the anchor.
2. **Graph `init.rs` test move, then R5:** `insta` snapshot of the rendered workflows first, then `src/templates/*.tmpl`.
3. **R1:** `insta` first only if coverage is thin, then owned stages with a single identity loop.
4. **R3:** snapshots of the intent and the operation-ID list first, then moves only.
5. **S3, then S2:** S2 as an `architecture.rs` rule plus a constructor taking the parsed global args. The two dry-run behaviors still need your decision.
6. **S1, S4, S5:** separate decisions.

The stack and its follow-ups are on `main`, but the release PR is stale, because the bot's latest refresh failed. I haven't diagnosed why, and I haven't touched #188.

**What I did this turn**
- **#189, tooling settings:** commits your checkout's settings as they are: Entire pushes checkpoints and sessions and summarizes, the `.claude` `SubagentStop` hook, and the slimmed `.gemini/settings.json`.
- **#190, scanner dedup:** `workspace_root`, the `src` walker and the test-module stripper now live once in `callisto-graph/tests/common/mod.rs`. Both architecture test binaries pass (9 tests) and clippy is clean.
- Both are against `main` and not drafts. I'll check their CI.

**The release PR**

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
  fi
  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
}
trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  :
else
  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
fi
staging_created=true

jq -n \
  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
  '{
    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
    variables: {
      input: {
        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
        message: {headline: $headline},
        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
        fileChanges: {
          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
        }
      }
    }
  }' > body.json

new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then

fi

command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \

  fi

trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.

fi

else

    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
  fi
fi
moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" \
    --applied-head "$new_sha" > /dev/null
else
  callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
fi

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;

content.text:
The one fix the release actually depends on is [#191](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/191). The other items are smaller cleanups, and the big product-safety defects are not touched. I haven't checked hosted CI on the new PRs yet.

**Fixes opened this turn**

| PR | What | In the release? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#191](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/191) | The release PR refresh failing with `E148` | Yes: it has a changeset |
| [#192](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/192) | Validating `GroupTable::try_from_groups`; `from_groups` deprecated, not changed | No changeset: it's a library addition and deprecation, with no CLI change |
| [#193](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/193) | Dry-run permits derived from the flag, plus an architecture test | No changeset: no behavior change |
| [#189](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/189) | Tooling settings, as you decided | No |
| [#190](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/190) | Scanner dedup | No |

#193 is stacked on #190. #189 was green when I last looked.

**E148 root cause and evidence**
- **Cause (inferred):** the update path failed about a second after the managed branch moved. The PR's `updatedAt` and a new CI event show the move succeeded. The best explanation is that `gh pr list` still returned the old head, which the post-update check reads as a changed snapshot. I couldn't observe the stale read directly.
- **Fix:** the final verification retries for up to 27 seconds. A head that never shows the applied commit still fails.
- **Test evidence:** a new contract case reproduces the failure on the old script and passes with the fix. A companion case confirms a real change still fails. The contract suite passes 22/22 under CI's minimal PATH.

**Corrections to the handoff**
- Qwen said `artifact-manifest --dry-run` writes a file, and that `init --dry-run` needed a contract decision. Both were wrong. All three permit sites were already safe by control flow, and a test confirms `artifact-manifest` rejects `--dry-run`. So #193 changes no behavior and needed none of the owner decisions.
- S3's "extract and share" also needed a tweak: raw config uses string names and `from_groups` uses resolved ids, so the shared core takes neutral name/member pairs.

**Not done**
- The V1-FINDINGS safety defects (`SYS-RETRY`, `SYS-PYFILES`, `SYS-BARRIER`, `SYS-MATURIN`, the T06–T09 work, D01) are untouched. They're design work and shouldn't be rushed into this release.
- Qwen's R1–R3 and R5 refactors, S1, S4 and S5 are not started either.
- #188 itself still needs a workflow approval from you. After #191 merges, a new release run will refresh it.

needs input: Do you want me to watch hosted CI on #189–#193 and report, or move on to one of the larger items (`SYS-RETRY` is the most user-visible)?

content.text:
The real gaps are in six feature areas. The drop itself is mostly a measurement artifact, as above: `walk.rs` has only 19 genuinely uncovered production lines, for example.

I read the line-level report and sorted the uncovered regions by what a user or attacker could actually hit. These are the ones worth black-box tests:

| # | Area | Uncovered behavior | Black-box scenario |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `release_decision.rs`: verifying the merged release commit (4 distinct `ReleaseCommitVerificationFailed` paths, plus selection errors) | Every rejection of a tampered release commit | `release plan --from-release-commit` on a commit with an extra changed file, a wrong decision digest, or a mismatched manifest version must be refused with the right error. This is ADR 2's authority check, and only the happy path is tested. |
| 2 | `cli/commands/release.rs`: `artifact-manifest` | `ReleaseNoArtifactSlots`, not-a-regular-file, symlink and path-escape rejections | Real files in a temp dir: a symlinked, directory-escaping and missing asset must each be rejected. This is path containment, so it matters most for security. |
| 3 | `cascade.rs` | Exact-pinned dependencies, unresolvable specs (catalog, opaque), and the diagnostics they emit | A workspace with `=1.2.3` pins and a pnpm catalog dependency: version must rewrite the pin and report that the catalog spec can't be evaluated. |
| 4 | `manifests/cargo.rs` | Version write into an inline-table dependency, path dependencies | A Cargo manifest with `dep = { version = "…", path = "…" }`: the bump rewrites only the version and keeps every byte of formatting. This is the format-preservation invariant. |
| 5 | `apply.rs` | poetry and pdm lock refresh (only uv is covered), and staging a modified path that no longer exists | The runner seam is the black-box boundary: assert the exact `poetry lock --no-update` and `pdm` commands. CI doesn't have those tools installed. |
| 6 | `cli/commands/release.rs` JSON output | `--format json` for the release and plan reports, and warning output | Parse the JSON envelope and check the receipt fields. It also feeds the schema guards. |

- **Skip:** most remaining uncovered lines are error-mapping boilerplate (`detail: error.to_string()`), unreachable defensive arms, and trait accessors. Testing them only moves the number.
- **Refactor link:** the `apply.rs` items (5) double as the safety net before R2. The duplicated git-command and error-mapping blocks at `apply.rs:528-565` are also what R2 unifies.
- **Priority:** 1 and 2 first, since they guard release authority and path safety. Then 4, 3 and 5.

content.text:
All six test groups are written and committed on `test/black-box-gaps`, and one of them found a real bug. The full `just ci` is running. R2 starts after it, because cargo builds can't run in parallel.

**What the tests cover**

| Group | New tests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Release-commit verification | 6 (`release_commit_verification_tests.rs`) | Each tamper (stale decision, no changeset consumed, no changelog, manifest not in the diff, wrong version) is rejected with `E165` and its own specific reason. |
| 2. `artifact-manifest` | 6 (`release_artifact_manifest_tests.rs`) | Symlinked, directory and missing assets are refused with no manifest written, and unlisted files are ignored. The `E222` path-escape branch can't be reached through the CLI, so I left it as defense in depth. |
| 3. Cascade | 5 (`cascade_scenarios_tests.rs`) | Exact pins, a pnpm catalog spec reported but not rewritten, and a stale linked-group member rejected with `E108`. |
| 4. Cargo format preservation | included above | Inline-table dependencies in `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and target tables, rewritten with comments and layout kept byte for byte. |
| 5. Lockfile refresh | 2 | Poetry (`poetry lock --no-update`), plus "exactly one Python lockfile refreshed, in uv, poetry, pdm order". |
| 6. JSON output | 1 | "Nothing to release" is a typed JSON envelope for both the preview and the real run. |

**The bug the tests found**

- **Symptom:** a version bump rewrote `[dependencies]` and `[dev-dependencies]` but left `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` on the old pin. `cargo update` then failed with `E208` and the workspace was broken.
- **Worse variant:** a package that depends on a sibling only through a target table was invisible to the graph and never released.
- **Cause:** the Cargo manifest only read and rewrote the three top-level dependency tables.
- **Fix:** it now covers target-specific tables too, reporting each (kind, name) once. It includes a changeset.
- **Verification:** the two tests for it fail on the old code and pass with the fix.

**Corrections to earlier claims**
- The stale linked-group member warning in `cascade.rs` can't be reached, since config loading rejects it first.
- uv and pdm were already covered, and only poetry was missing.

The CI log will show whether coverage moved.

I'll open the PR once `just ci` passes, then start R2 with these tests as its safety net.

content.text:
R2 is done locally on `refactor/apply-pipeline`, stacked on #195 (the tests PR). The full `just ci` is running before I commit and open the PR.

**What changed in `apply.rs`**
- **Function size:** `apply_version_plan` is 123 lines, down from 447.
- **Ordered write steps:** `write_steps` classifies every manifest write once into an ordered list of steps. The per-file order (bump, then rewrites, then exactly one persist) is now data. `apply_write_step` is a single `match` executor that returns the path to stage. The old "iterate all bumps, `continue` if not excluded" loops are gone.
- **Shared helpers:**
  - `open_canonical` replaces five copies of the open-a-manifest ceremony.
  - `write_version_guarded` replaces three copies of the from/to idempotency check.
  - `run_git_on_paths` replaces three copies of the git call and its error mapping.
  - `active_ecosystems` is now a pure function.
  - `refresh_lockfiles` holds the per-package-manager refresh.

**Evidence it's a pure move**
- All 849 graph tests and all 420 CLI tests pass unchanged, including the byte-identity tests and the new poetry and precedence tests.
- Clippy is clean, and the public `apply_version_plan` signature is unchanged.

I'll report the full `just ci` result and open the PR when it lands.

/usr/bin/git add crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs && /usr/bin/git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(graph): classify apply writes once and run them through one executor

apply_version_plan is 123 lines instead of 447. Manifest writes are ordered once into steps whose per-file order (bump, then rewrites, then one persist) is data, and a single match executes them, replacing the loops that iterated the whole plan and skipped what another loop owned. Opening a manifest, the from/to idempotency guard, the git calls and the active-ecosystem set each live in one helper.
EOF
/usr/bin/git push -q -u origin refactor/apply-pipeline 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --base test/black-box-gaps --head refactor/apply-pipeline --title "refactor(graph): classify apply writes once and run them through one executor" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`apply_version_plan` was 447 lines with the same primitives copied through it: opening a canonical manifest five times, the from/to idempotency guard three times, and the git call with its error mapping three times. Several loops also iterated the whole plan only to `continue` past writes another loop owned.

Manifest writes are now classified once into an ordered list of steps (`write_steps`) and executed by a single `match` (`apply_write_step`), so the per-file order (version bump first, then every dependency rewrite, then exactly one persist) is data rather than control flow. The order of steps is the order the old loops ran: batched manifests, workspace roots, mixed-routing versions, mixed-routing rewrites, platform writes, optional dependencies. `open_canonical`, `write_version_guarded` (the idempotency precondition that makes a retry safe), `run_git_on_paths`, `active_ecosystems` and `refresh_lockfiles` each live once. `apply_version_plan` is 123 lines.

No behavior change. The existing byte-identity tests pass unchanged, along with the poetry and lockfile-precedence tests added in the stacked-under PR; the graph (849) and CLI (420) suites and `just ci` pass with the same 1,882 tests. The public `apply_version_plan` signature is unchanged.

Stacked on #195. No user-facing change, so no changeset.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

From Codex: 

<pasted_content id="3f57">
I reviewed all seven open PRs against their current bases, the architecture docs, and the repo rules. I found one code blocker and one release gate blocker.

### Findings

1. High — #195 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/195) collapses distinct Cargo target dependencies. The new dependency iterator (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/525b17ef47d7bec32cbc6da8161bada9a0587479/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs#L393) reports only the first declaration for each (kind, name), while the rewrite (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/525b17ef47d7bec32cbc6da8161bada9a0587479/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs#L480) changes every declaration with that key. A top-level dependency and a target dependency can use the same local name but refer to different packages or have different version constraints. Bumping one can then rewrite the other’s pin; the graph can also miss the other package entirely. Workspace inheritance is tracked by the same coarse key, so one inherited target declaration can cause a direct declaration to be treated as inherited. Keep target declarations distinct through graph construction and rewriting, and test differing aliases, constraints, and inheritance.
2. High — #188 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/188) has no CI checks and GitHub reports it as UNSTABLE. This is the generated PR whose merge publishes version 0.10.1. The repo’s CI workflow (.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:4) covers PRs to main, but no check run is attached to this PR. Run the required validation on its exact head before merging.
3. Low — #192 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/192) rejects a valid platform-only group through its new constructor. The constructor (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/46d58c9/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs) validates only package_members(), making a group containing a platform manifest appear empty. The config resolution path accepts that member shape. Validate all members while checking package ownership separately.

### PR assessment

| PR | Assessment |
|---|---|
| #196 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/196) | Apply refactor follows the prior write order and retains the guarded version writes. No separate defect found; it is stacked on #195. |
| #195 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/195) | Request changes for the Cargo target dependency issue. Its new black-box tests cover matching declarations, not differing ones. |
| #193 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/193) | No issue found. Permit construction now uses the parsed dry-run flag; stacked on #190. |
| #192 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/192) | Fix the platform-only constructor case before treating the new API as equivalent to config loading. |
| #191 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/191) | No issue found. The retry retains final verification and has success and failure coverage. |
| #190 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/190) | No issue found. The shared scanner preserves the prior helpers’ behavior. |
| #188 (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/188) | Hold merge until its exact release commit has passing checks. |

The completed checks for #190–#193 and #191 passed when queried; the macOS tests for #195 and #196 were still running. This was a diff and execution-path review; I did not run local Cargo tests against the PR heads or post review comments.
</pasted_content id="3f57">
